what_worked: Consistent visual template with clear key-takeaway boxes on every slide; readable hierarchy.
fix_next: Nearly every quantitative claim appears fabricated—categories, percentages, medians, and geographic splits don't match the dataset at all.
verdict: Polished template over fabricated numbers; not a data story.
factual_error_detail: Slide 3: '6,000+ startups' — dataset has 1,000 rows; '85%+ revenue-validated' unsupported. Slide 4: Category percentages (35% SaaS & Productivity, 28% AI, 15% Mobile Apps, 12% Creator Tools, 10% Ecommerce) don't match dataset categories or counts; 274 rows have missing category. Slide 5: 'Subscriptions 65%' revenue share is a fabricated category not in the dataset; AI actual share is ~15.1% not 20%; Mobile Apps ~1.5% not 10%. Slide 6: AI median '$2K–$5K' — actual AI median is $503; SaaS median '$8K–$25K' — actual is $200.50; 'top 5% generate 40%' — actual top-10 (top 1%) share is 49.6%, so 5%/40% is plausible but unverified. Slide 7: Geographic percentages entirely fabricated — dataset has country missing for 241 rows and no 'Western Europe' or 'Canada' aggregation provided. Slide 8: Stripe 72% — actual is 63.6%; RevenueCat 12% — actual ~18.9%; Polar 8% — actual ~3.6%. Slide 6 key takeaway 'inversely correlated' is a misuse of the term.

evidence.insight: Claims like 'popularity ≠ value' and 'maturity gap' are interesting framings but rest on fabricated numbers, so insights are hollow. No original analysis of missingness, anonymity premium, or founded-year correlation.
evidence.narrative: There is a loose arc from business model → composition → revenue → geography → infrastructure → strategy, but it reads as a marketing pitch for TrustMRR rather than a critical data story. No thesis is tested.
evidence.framing: Slide 1-2 set context but never define the dataset (1,000-row sample), never mention missingness (241 country, 274 category, 288 audience_type), and never state limitations. A cold reader would think this covers 6,000+ companies.
evidence.accuracy: Almost every quantitative claim is wrong relative to the frozen dataset. Categories are renamed/merged without disclosure. Medians are off by 4–50x. Provider shares are wrong. Geographic data appears invented. Revenue category chart uses 'Subscriptions' which is not a dataset category.
evidence.visual: Consistent dark teal + coral palette, legible typography, donut/bar charts are clean. But charts encode fabricated data, and the donut-chart-heavy approach (3 donuts) becomes repetitive. Decorative clip-art (slide 1-2, slide 9) adds no analytical value.
evidence.ai_slop: Heavy AI-generated feel: decorative clip-art, identical slide templates, inflated consulting language ('category of one,' 'network effects'), round fabricated percentages (35/28/15/12/10), and no evidence of actual data analysis.
